versions.changelog: Verified against the latest release of every supported product — each one was re-tested end to end: create a real session, fork it, then let the product read the branch back itself. Hermes 0.21.6 raised its session-store version from 30 to 31, which the adapter used to refuse; both are accepted now, anything newer is still refused. Also fixed: a branch no longer inherits the source session's auto-archive flag.

The bundle you install no longer carries build-time bytecode caches — those files embed our machine's absolute paths, so packaging now refuses to publish if any is left behind. Also fixes a wall of decode errors when building from source on Chinese Windows.
Every doc now states only its own channel's entry point: the previously contradictory instructions are gone, and reader-facing wording no longer carries internal jargon. No runtime behavior change.

Wording and naming cleanup, no functional change: source comments and docs now state only this tool's own technical rationale; the test script uses a more conventional name (regress_samples); and a local-only validation script is no longer shipped with the repository. No behavior change for users.

Until now, simply using a branch made fork --verify report a permanent failure and tell you to fix it before publishing — even when the content was entirely normal (for example, writing down which session the branch came from). This release separates the two: residue inside the engine-copied prefix still blocks, while anything appended after the snapshot point is only flagged for review and no longer affects the exit code, with a breakdown of what landed in message text versus tool output or reasoning. New branches also carry a prefix fingerprint, so the check can prove that region is still byte-for-byte what fork wrote (older branches have none, and will say so — that is missing evidence, not an error). A single unparseable line no longer aborts the whole check either: it is skipped and reported with its line number.

Windows now works: previously the very first command crashed there, because the output encoding could not hold Chinese or emoji. This release fixes it, adds a platform section to the skill doc (use 'py -3' on Windows; PowerShell execution policy; WSL vs native session stores), corrects a dependency declaration that made the skill look unsatisfied on Windows, and makes Python 3.9 actually supported as previously claimed.

This release fixes places where the docs said one thing and the code did another: the --dry-run description contradicted itself (one place said 'zero writes', another said it writes a temp file - the code does the latter), now unified in all three places; machine-readable permission fields added; a language switcher is now in the skill doc (English readers previously had no entry point); and side-effect notices can no longer be silenced.

No new features — this release is about being explicit: installs are now pinned to a release tag (you get the exact version you chose, not whatever main happens to be), a new 'Data & permission boundaries' section states exactly which files it touches, a doc contradiction that could make you run the wrong command is fixed, and file-writing actions now print a human-readable notice.
一条被截断的 emoji 以前能让整条会话打不出分支，且报错指不到任何地方——本版起能正常打分支：只有那一行改用 JSON 转义，其余内容逐字不变；6 个产品后端全部覆盖。
